Contributing to vellumwidget

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Build and test

The runtime is TypeScript in srcts/, bundled into the committed inst/htmlwidgets/vellumwidget.js with npm run build (node esbuild.js). Commit the rebuilt bundle with every source change: the js-runtime CI job rebuilds it and fails when the committed copy is stale. Before a PR, run

  • npx tsc --noEmit and node tests/js/behavior.test.js (jsdom), and
  • devtools::test() for the R side.

A PR that needs an unmerged vellum or vellumplot change

vellumwidget’s CI installs vellum and vellumplot from their GitHub main (the Remotes: field in DESCRIPTION). A widget PR that builds on a vellum PR that has not been merged yet would therefore run against the old vellum, and the tests that feature-detect the new vellum would skip.

To check such a PR against the vellum branch, put a line like this in the PR description (on its own line, anywhere in the text):

vellum-ref: my-feature-branch

vellumplot-ref: works the same way for vellumplot. The value is a branch, tag or full commit SHA on r-vellum/vellum (r-vellum/vellumplot). The R-CMD-check workflow reads the description when it runs, installs the dependencies from main as usual, then builds and installs that ref over them, in the CI job only: nothing is committed, so there is nothing to undo when the PR merges. The job log shows a notice naming the ref and commit it built against.

  • Editing the description does not start a new run: re-run the R-CMD-check job (it reads the description afresh).
  • Merge the vellum PR first. Then delete the vellum-ref: line and re-run the widget PR’s check, so it passes against vellum’s main before you merge it. (If the branch was deleted with the merge, the job warns and falls back to main anyway.)
  • Pushes to main and the nightly run always use main.
